leadText:
A Youngster (Japanese: / Shorts Youngster, shortened in Generation I to たんパン Shorts) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that debuted in the Generation I games. They are depicted as average young boys usually wearing caps and short pants.

They use a variety of Pokémon, but they tend to use common ones that are caught early in their respective games. In Unova and Kalos, a significant amount of Youngsters specialize in Pokémon, likely due to the absence of the class in those regions. Some will give out Ultra Balls when defeated. In the Battle Maison, they specialize in Bug- and Pokémon.

Youngsters appear to be the male counterparts of es.

In Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, Youngsters will award three s along with prize money upon being defeated, except for Master Trainers.

In Pokémon Stadium, they are referred to as Lads.

===Pokémon Adventures===
 
==== ====
 

Joey is Professor Elm's assistant and his errand boy. His partner is . In Chuang Yi's translations of the manga, he was known as Grant. However, VIZ Media's translations properly identify him as Joey.

==== ====
In Epilogue, Joey makes a cameo appearance in one of the ships heading to the .

==== ====
A Youngster is seen amongst the many people visiting the in Weavile Wobbles But It Won't Fall Down.

==== ====
A Youngster appears in A Conk on Cranidos's Cranium, where he serves as 's first opponent at the Oreburgh Gym.

 
==== ====
A Youngster appears in Softening Up Kakuna as a challenger of the . In the battle shown, he rents a , , and Trash Cloak , later trading the Wormadam for a . Another Youngster appeared in Clobbering Claydol, wandering around the .

==== ====
A Youngster with a appeared in An Odd Speech, listening to Ghetsis's speech but ultimately disregarding what he said about releasing his Pokémon.

A Youngster with a is seen in Dream a Little Dream amongst the many Trainers entering .

Leo, a boy wearing a combination of Youngster and clothes, appears as a recurring character in both Black & White and .

==== ====
In An X-cuse to Come Out and Play, a Youngster was seen fleeing from a battle between and .

In Sylveon Enchants, a Youngster was seen in the Mini-game Corner with his .

A Youngster appeared in Trevenant Pokes with his younger brother, a , at the Tower of Mastery before deciding to go home.

A Youngster appeared in Diantha's flashback in Pinsir Glares.

==== ====
In Truth and the Mastermind Behind Team Skull, someone was heard calling for Youngster Tyler at Hokulani Observatory.

==== ====
A Youngster with a appeared in Henry Sword's fantasy in Zap!! A Rising Beam of Light, where he explained to Casey Shield that they would need a nickname for Marvin's Sobble to avoid confusion in case another Trainer had the same Pokémon.

==In the TCG==
 
 
Youngster was introduced as a in the Pokémon Trading Card Game during the English Scarlet & Violet Series (the Japanese Scarlet & Violet Era). It was first released in the Japanese and the English expansion, with artwork by Hitoshi Ariga. It lets the player shuffle their hand into their deck, and draw five cards.
 

==Trivia==
In Pokémon GO, "Youngster" is the name of an achievement awarded for catching at least 3 tiny .
In Pokémon Champions, the title of "Youngster" is awarded for winning ten battles using Pokémon.
